summary: Follow-up plan of layer RD.2 (local monodromy with Frobenius) of the roadmap 'P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights'. It plans what the accepted first pass left open, citing that pass's 30 RD.2 nodes instead of repeating them. Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem, imported there, is now proved from public sources along Kedlaya's p-adic Differential Equations, Chapter 19: the unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and Ẽ of the Amice ring with their Galois action; the unit-root modules D(V) and D†(V) of Galois representations and the Fontaine-Katz equivalence; Lang trivialisation modulo π^m, which produces the finite separable extension over which the Frobenius matrix is within c of the identity (the step Kedlaya's Proposition 6.11 assumes); c-constant modules and the normal form of their matrices; Dwork's transfer theorem to the centre of a disc; the key lemma that c-constancy with c < p^{−1/(p−1)} forces triviality (sharp, by Dwork's module); and Tsuzuki's theorem in trivialisation and equivalence form. Chapter 4 of Kedlaya's overview, which the RD.1 pass assigned here, gives the description of quasi-constant modules by semilinear representations and Matsuda's decomposition with local duality. Chapter 5 gives the behaviour of highest breaks under tame and Artin-Schreier covers, Matsuda's theorem that the highest break of a quasi-unipotent module is the highest ramification break of its monodromy, and the identification of break decompositions, so that the differential Swan conductor equals the Galois Swan conductor. André's Tannakian form is planned over the algebraic closure K̄: every quasi-unipotent module admits a Frobenius structure, so MCF(R_K̄/K̄) is the category of quasi-unipotent modules; the logarithmic fibre functor identifies it with representations of I × G_a, Tau Ceti's comodule reconstruction gives the Tannakian group I × G_a, its wild part is P, and the tame factor is the nilpotent residue, with solution spaces dual to coker N. The local monodromy theorem is stated over every finite étale extension R^L of the Robba ring and for rings presented as such, which is the analytic input of Berger's theorem without any p-adic Hodge theory in this layer. The completion of an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed in every characteristic (placed in RD.0, where the extended Robba ring uses it). The published Documenta version of Slope filtrations revisited and its erratum were read: a label concordance and the erratum's corrections are recorded.

nodes.title: Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring
nodes.statement: Fix a separable closure k((t))^sep of k((t)) and put G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))). (a) For each finite separable extension L ⊆ k((t))^sep of k((t)) there is a finite étale O_E-algebra O_{E_L}, unique up to unique isomorphism, with O_{E_L}/π ≅ L; E_L = O_{E_L}[1/π] is a complete discretely valued field with residue field L. Its integral elements overconvergent over R^int form the finite étale R^int-algebra R^int_L of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring, and E†_L := R^int_L[1/π] = R^bd_L is the unique finite unramified extension of the henselian field E† with residue field L; moreover E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L and E†_L is the integral closure of E† in E_L. (b) E^unr = ∪_L E_L and E^{†,unr} = ∪_L E†_L (union over finite separable L ⊆ k((t))^sep), and Ẽ is the π-adic completion of E^unr: a complete discretely valued field with residue field k((t))^sep. The Frobenius lift σ and the derivation d extend uniquely to O_{E_L}, R^int_L, E_L, E†_L, E^unr, E^{†,unr} and (by continuity) Ẽ, and G acts on all of them by continuous ring automorphisms commuting with σ and d, with fixed rings (E^unr)^{G_L} = E_L, (E^{†,unr})^{G_L} = E†_L, Ẽ^G = E and (E^{†,unr})^G = E†, where G_L = Gal(k((t))^sep/L). (c) Constants: the kernel of d on E†_L is the integral closure K_L of K in E†_L (a finite unramified extension of K whose residue field is the algebraic closure of k in L), and the kernel of d on Ẽ is the completion K̃ of the maximal unramified extension of K in Ẽ. (d) Frobenius invariants: if σ_K is absolute (it acts on k by x ↦ x^q) and its fixed field K_0 = K^{σ_K = 1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K, then Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; L ranges over finite separable extensions of k((t)) inside one fixed separable closure. No perfectness of k is needed for (a)-(c); a purely inseparable residue extension k((t^{1/p}))/k((t)) has no étale lift.

In (d) the hypotheses are those of Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Proposition 19.1.5; without them Ẽ^{σ=1} can be smaller than K^{σ_K=1}·(unramified constants) and the coefficient field of the Fontaine-Katz equivalence changes.
proofSteps: (a) O_E is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k((t)) and R^int is henselian with the same residue field (RD.0/bounded-robba-ring (a)), so finite separable extensions of the residue field lift uniquely to finite étale algebras of either (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 15.1.3 and Definition 19.2.1); O_{E_L} is the π-adic completion of R^int_L, which gives E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L, and the integral closure statement follows because R^int_L is normal and finite over R^int.

(b) Unique extension of σ and d: an étale algebra over a ring with an endomorphism or derivation carries a unique compatible extension (the residue map of σ is the q-power map, which extends to L because L/k((t)) is separable). G acts on E^unr by transport of structure through the equivalence between finite separable extensions of k((t)) and finite étale algebras, and continuously on the completion; fixed rings by Galois theory for finite étale algebras (Kedlaya, Definition 19.1.1, p. 314).

(c) A d-constant x of E†_L is integral over K: reduce to a field extension and use that d has kernel K on E† (power series with i·c_i = 0 for i ≠ 0, RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring) and that d commutes with the trace of E†_L/E†; the kernel on Ẽ is Kedlaya, Exercise 19.3, p. 325.

(d) Kedlaya, Exercise 19.1, p. 325: reduce to residue fields, where the fixed field of the q-power map on k((t))^sep is F_q; the value-group hypothesis gives a uniformiser of K fixed by σ, so σ-invariant elements can be expanded π-adically with σ-invariant digits.
acceptance: For L = k((t)): E_L = E, E†_L = E† and the Galois action is trivial.
For an unramified L = k'((t)) with k'/k finite separable: E†_L = E† ⊗_K K' with K'/K unramified of residue field k', and ker(d) = K'.

Artin-Schreier: if K contains π_0 with π_0^{p−1} = −p, then E†[u]/((1 + π_0 u)^p − 1 − pπ_0 t^{−1}) is the unramified extension E†_L for L = k((t))[ū]/(ū^p − ū + t^{−1}) (expand (1 + π_0 u)^p and divide by pπ_0; compare Kedlaya overview, proof of Lemma 5.4.7).

nodes.title: c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules
nodes.statement: For c ∈ (0, 1), a finite free differential module M over E† (or over E, or over E†_L for a finite separable L/k((t))) equipped with a unit-root Frobenius structure F relative to σ is c-constant if M has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A with entries in the integral ring and |A − I|_1 ≤ c, where |·|_1 is the 1-Gauss norm (the π-adic norm on E). Such a basis is a c-constant basis. Properties: (i) the property does not depend on the Frobenius lift: if σ_1, σ_2 are Frobenius lifts that agree on K, the Frobenius structure transported along the Taylor isomorphism of RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures is c-constant for σ_2 iff the original one is c-constant for σ_1; (ii) c-constancy is preserved by base change E† → E†_L → E_L, by tensor products and by duals, and c-constant implies c'-constant for c ≤ c' < 1; (iii) if σ is absolute and K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} satisfies the hypotheses of RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (d), then D(V) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module) is c-constant iff V_0 has a G-stable O_{K_0}-lattice whose supremum norm satisfies |τ(g)x − x| ≤ c|x| for all g ∈ G.
hypotheses: The Frobenius structure is unit-root: there is a basis on which F acts by A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)).
c is measured in the normalised absolute value of K extended to E by the 1-Gauss norm.
proofSteps: (i) Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Definition 19.3.2 and Exercise (5) of Chapter 19: in Lemma 17.3.4, the integral lattice M_0 spanned by a basis on which F acts integrally is stable under D^i/i!, and if D/i acts with norm at most c on a suitable basis so does D^i/i!; inserting this into the Taylor formula (17.3.1.1) for the transported Frobenius structure gives a matrix A' with |A' − I|_1 ≤ c (|σ_2(t) − σ_1(t)|_1 < 1).
(ii) Base change keeps the same basis; for tensor products A ⊗ B − I = (A − I) ⊗ B + I ⊗ (B − I) and for duals (A^T)^{-1} − I = −(A^T)^{-1}(A − I)^T, with |A^{-1}|_1 = 1.

(iii) Kedlaya, Definition 19.3.2: through the Fontaine-Katz equivalence (RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence), a c-constant basis of D(V) corresponds to a G-stable lattice of V_0 on which G acts by matrices congruent to I to within c.
acceptance: The trivial module (E†, d) with F = σ is c-constant for every c: A = (1).
Rank one: M = E† e with F(e) = a e, ∇e = 0 and a ∈ 1 + π^m O_K is |π|^m-constant (the compatibility N a + t da/dt = q a σ(N) holds with N = 0 because a is constant).

Dwork's module (K = Q_p(π_0), π_0^{p−1} = −p, σ_K = id, σ(t) = t^p): M_f = E† v with ∇v = −π_0 (df/dt) v ⊗ dt, f = t^{−1}, and F(v) = E(t^{−1}) v with E(z) = exp(π_0(z − z^p)) = Σ λ_n z^n the Dwork exponential (this sign of the connection is the one that matches F; Kedlaya's Example 17.1.4 prints +π_0, source issue E-RD2-12; the dual module is E_π of RD.1/dwork-exponential-module, with F = E(t^{−1})^{−1}); since λ_n ∈ Z_p[π_0] with λ_1 = π_0 and ord_p λ_n ≥ n(p − 1)/p² > 0 for n ≥ 1 (RD.1/dwork-overconvergence-proof, RD.1/dwork-exponential-module), E(t^{−1}) ≡ 1 (mod π_0) and |E(t^{−1}) − 1|_1 = |π_0| = p^{−1/(p−1)}, so M_f is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant; it is not trivial over E† (its horizontal section exp(π_0 t^{−1})v does not converge near |t| = 1), hence by RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial it is not c-constant for any c < p^{−1/(p−1)}: the threshold is sharp.

nodes.title: Unit-root Frobenius modules are trivialised over Ẽ, and become c-constant over a finite separable extension
nodes.statement: Setting of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring: K is complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with ring of integers O_K, uniformiser π and residue field k of characteristic p; σ is a Frobenius lift on R^int (a ring endomorphism extending a q-power Frobenius lift σ_K of K and reducing to the absolute q-power map x ↦ x^q of k((t))), q = p^a; E = O_E[1/π] is the Amice ring and E† = R^bd the bounded Robba ring, both with d = d/dt. Let M_0 be a finite free R^int-module (or O_E-module) of rank n with a σ-semilinear F whose linearisation σ^*M_0 → M_0 is an isomorphism (an étale lattice of a unit-root σ-module). Then: (a) M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ has a basis of F-fixed vectors, and (M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ)^{F=1} is a free module of rank n over O_Ẽ^{σ=1}; (b) for each m ≥ 1 the set of F-fixed vectors of M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ/π^m is finite, and each of them is fixed by an open subgroup of G; (c) consequently, for each m ≥ 1 there is a finite Galois extension L of k((t)) such that M_0 ⊗ R^int_L has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A ≡ I (mod π^m). In particular every unit-root (σ,∇)-module M over E† becomes c-constant (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module) over E†_L for any prescribed c ∈ (0,1) and a suitable finite separable L/k((t)) depending on c.
hypotheses: Only the residual behaviour of σ is used: its reduction is the q-power map of k((t)), which extends to the q-power map of the separably closed field k((t))^sep. No perfectness of k and no condition on σ_K are needed.
A unit-root σ-module over E† has an étale R^int-lattice (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)).
proofSteps: Modulo π: M_0/π is an étale q-power Frobenius module over k((t)); over k((t))^sep its F-fixed vectors span and form an F_q-space of dimension n (Lang's theorem; the p-power, Z_p-coefficient case is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring (i), and the q-power case is the same argument applied to F, whose fixed-point equations X^{(q)} = A^{−1}X are étale of degree q^n).

Lifting: if v is F-fixed modulo π^j, write F v − v = π^j w; a correction v + π^j y is F-fixed modulo π^{j+1} iff ȳ − ū^j·F̄(ȳ) = w̄ modulo π, where σ(π) = uπ (indeed F(v + π^j y) − v − π^j y = π^j(w + u^j F(y) − y)); in coordinates this is a system x − c·x^{(q)} = b over k((t))^sep, separable (derivative 1) and solvable with finitely many solutions. Completeness of O_Ẽ gives F-fixed lifts and Nakayama's lemma gives a basis (a); this is Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 19.1.5 (via the first part of Theorem 14.6.3, the residue field of Ẽ being separably closed).
(b) Each level is cut out by finitely many étale polynomial equations, so the solutions are finite in number and algebraic and separable over k((t)); hence each is fixed by an open subgroup of G.

(c) Let L be the Galois closure of the field generated by the coordinates of an F-fixed basis modulo π^m. Since R^int_L/π^m = O_{E_L}/π^m (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (a)), the basis lifts to a basis of M_0 ⊗ R^int_L, on which F acts by A ≡ I (mod π^m). Choose m with |π|^m ≤ c (Kedlaya, proof of Theorem 19.3.1, p. 321, where L is chosen to make M c-constant).
acceptance: Rank one: for M_0 = R^int e with F(e) = a e, a ∈ (R^int)^×, a fixed vector b e needs b^{−1}σ(b) = a^{−1}; modulo π this is b̄^{q−1} = ā^{−1}, solvable over the finite separable extension k((t))(b̄) (the polynomial x^{q−1} − ā^{−1} is separable).

Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}, K = Q_p(π_0), π_0^{p−1} = −p) is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant over E† itself and becomes trivial, hence c-constant for every c, over E†_L for the Artin-Schreier extension L of z^p − z = t^{−1} (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example).

nodes.title: Unit-root differential modules D(V), D†(V) attached to Galois representations; finite local monodromy
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space and τ : G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) → GL(V) a continuous homomorphism. (a) (p-adic topology) D(V) := (V ⊗_K Ẽ)^G, with G acting diagonally, is an E-vector space of dimension dim_K V and D(V) ⊗_E Ẽ → V ⊗_K Ẽ is an isomorphism; d acting on the second factor makes D(V) a differential module over E, and any σ_K-semilinear bijection of V commuting with τ (for instance the one fixing a chosen basis) makes it a unit-root (σ,∇)-module for any Frobenius lift σ acting on K by σ_K. (b) (finite image) If τ factors through Gal(L/k((t))) for a finite Galois L, then D†(V) := (V ⊗_K E†_L)^G is an E†-vector space of dimension dim V, canonically independent of L, with D†(V) ⊗ E†_L ≅ V ⊗ E†_L and D†(V) ⊗_{E†} E = D(V); it is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E†. (c) τ has finite local monodromy if the image of the inertia subgroup I = Gal(k((t))^sep/k^sep((t))) is finite; then D†(V) is defined by the same formula with E^{†,sep} (the bounded Robba ring over the completion K̂^unr of the maximal unramified extension of K, in the variable t, with its unramified extensions) in place of E†_L, and is again a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† of rank dim V. (d) D†(V) is solvable at 1: its generic radius tends to 1 (RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability). (e) The horizontal sections of D†(V) ⊗_{E†} E†_L are V ⊗_K K_L (K_L = ker d on E†_L), so the differential structure recovers the restriction of V to inertia but not V itself.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; V finite-dimensional; τ continuous for the p-adic topology in (a), and with finite image (resp. finite image of inertia) in (b) (resp. (c)).
The Frobenius structure on D(V) comes from a chosen σ_K-semilinear structure on V; the differential structure needs no choice.
proofSteps: (a) Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 19.1.3: for finite image, Hilbert-Noether descent for the finite Galois extension E_L/E (Tau Ceti's semilinear Galois descent: invariant vectors span, TauCeti.GaloisDescent.span_invariants_eq_top, and stay independent, TauCeti.GaloisDescent.liftBaseChange_injective_of_invariant); in general choose a G-stable O_K-lattice T (compactness), apply the finite case to each T/m^i and pass to the inverse limit.

Differential and Frobenius structures: d and σ extend uniquely to Ẽ and commute with G (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (b)); they preserve invariants; the compatibility ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇ holds on V ⊗ Ẽ because d kills V and σ is a ring map (Definition 19.1.4).
(b) Same descent for E†_L/E† (Lemma 19.2.3); independence of L because enlarging L does not change invariants.

(c) Definition 19.2.8, which states the result without proof. Choose a finite Galois L/k((t)) with τ(I ∩ G_L) = 1 (possible because τ(I) is finite), so that τ restricted to G_L is unramified: it factors through G_L/(I ∩ G_L) = Gal(k^sep/k_L), k_L the residue field of L. The group Gal(k^sep/k_L) is infinite, so finite descent does not apply to it; instead the lattice argument of Lemma 19.1.3 for the complete field K̂^unr (a G_L-stable O_K-lattice, Hilbert-Noether descent modulo each power of π, passage to the limit) shows that V' = (V ⊗_K K̂^unr)^{G_L} is a K_L-form of V ⊗_K K̂^unr. Hence (V ⊗ E^{†,sep,unr})^{G_L} = V' ⊗_{K_L} E†_L, using (E^{†,sep,unr})^{G_L} = E†_L (coefficientwise Galois descent), and Hilbert-Noether descent for the finite group Gal(L/k((t))) acting on E†_L, as in (b), gives D†(V) of dimension dim V over E†.
(d) Proposition 19.2.5: the Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 (Theorem 17.2.1 = RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability).
(e) Remark 19.2.7, using ker(d on E†_L) = K_L (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (c)).
acceptance: Trivial V = K: D(V) = E and D†(V) = E† with F = σ and ∇ = d.

Artin-Schreier character (Kedlaya Example 19.2.6): with π_0^{p−1} = −p and ζ_p ≡ 1 − π_0 (mod π_0^2), the character of Gal(L/k((t))), L: z^p − z = f, sending z ↦ z + 1 to ζ_p has D†(V) ≅ Dwork's module M_f (∇v = −π_0 (df/dt) v ⊗ dt, with the sign of source issue E-RD2-12).
An unramified character (finite image of Frobenius only): D†(V) is trivial as a differential module but its Frobenius structure is the twist by the character's value on Frobenius.

nodes.title: Fontaine-Katz equivalence: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E and p-adic representations of G_{k((t))}
nodes.statement: Suppose σ_K is absolute (it acts on k by x ↦ x^q) and its fixed field K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K. For a continuous representation V_0 of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) on a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space, give V = V_0 ⊗_{K_0} K the σ_K-semilinear Frobenius fixing V_0. Then V_0 ↦ D(V) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (a)) is an equivalence, compatible with tensor products and duals, from continuous K_0-representations of G to finite differential modules over E with a unit-root Frobenius structure relative to σ; a quasi-inverse is D ↦ (D ⊗_E Ẽ)^{F=1}. Moreover the differential structure is redundant: a finite free unit-root σ-module over E carries a unique compatible differential structure. For K = Q_q and σ_K the q-power Witt-vector Frobenius (the identity of Q_q) this is an equivalence with continuous Q_q-representations of G_{F_q((t))} (Kedlaya, Corollary 19.1.6).
hypotheses: σ is a Frobenius lift on E acting on K by σ_K, with σ_K absolute; the value-group and residue-field hypotheses on K_0 guarantee Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0 (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (d)).

For Z_p-lattices and a p-power Frobenius on a Cohen ring this is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring (ii); here the coefficients are O_{K_0} and the Frobenius has order q.
proofSteps: D(V) is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (a)).
(D(V_0) ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} = (V ⊗_K Ẽ)^{F=1} = V_0 ⊗_{K_0} Ẽ^{σ=1} = V_0, using Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0 (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 19.1.5, and Exercise (1) of Chapter 19).

For D unit-root, D ⊗ Ẽ is a trivial difference module: it has a basis of F-fixed vectors (RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules (a)); hence V_0(D) := (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} has K_0-dimension rank D, the natural map V_0(D) ⊗ Ẽ → D ⊗ Ẽ is an isomorphism, G acts continuously on V_0(D) by (b) of that lemma, and D(V_0(D)) = D by taking G-invariants (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (b)).

Uniqueness of the differential structure (Kedlaya, Exercise (2) of Chapter 19 and Remark 19.1.7): under D ⊗ Ẽ ≅ V_0 ⊗ Ẽ any compatible connection kills the F-fixed vectors, because ∇ maps (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} into the F-fixed part of D ⊗ Ẽ ⊗ Ω^1, which is zero: an F-fixed element Σ v_i ⊗ a_i dt (v_i an F-fixed basis) satisfies a_i = σ(a_i)·dσ(t)/dt, and since σ is isometric on Ẽ and |dσ(t)/dt|_1 ≤ |π| (RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring) this forces a_i = 0; so ∇ = 1 ⊗ d on V_0 ⊗ Ẽ, and it descends uniquely.
Tensor compatibility: F-fixed vectors of a tensor product contain the tensor products of F-fixed vectors, with equal dimensions.
acceptance: V_0 = K_0 trivial ↦ (E, d, σ).

Corollary 19.1.6: for K = Q_q and σ_K = id (the q-power Witt Frobenius), continuous Q_q-representations of G_{F_q((t))} correspond to unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E for a Frobenius lift with σ(t) ≡ t^q.

nodes.title: Normal form of the matrices of a unit-root (σ,∇)-module for a standard Frobenius lift
nodes.statement: Let σ be a standard Frobenius lift on E† (σ(t) = t^q; σ_K arbitrary) and M a finite free differential module over E† with a unit-root Frobenius structure. Then there is an integer m ≥ 1 prime to p such that M ⊗_{E†} E†[t^{1/m}] has a basis on which the matrices A, A^{−1} of F and N of t·d/dt have entries in E†[t^{1/m}] ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1/m}⟧ (power series in t^{−1/m} with integral coefficients and no positive powers of t). If M is c-constant for some c < 1 (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module), one may take m = 1 and keep |A − I|_1 ≤ c.
hypotheses: σ standard: σ(t) = t^q and σ extends σ_K on K; the Frobenius structure is unit-root (a basis with A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) exists).
E†[t^{1/m}] is the bounded Robba ring in the variable t^{1/m}, a tamely ramified extension of E†.
proofSteps: Choose a basis on which A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)); reorder so that the minimum t-adic valuation of the reduction of the entries occurs in position (1,1), adjoin t^{1/(q−1)} and rescale to make it 0, then eliminate the rest of the first column; proceeding inductively makes A upper triangular and invertible over k⟦t^{1/m}⟧ modulo π (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 19.3.3, first paragraph of the proof).

Write A = Σ_i A_i t^{i/m}; repeatedly replace A by U^{−1} A σ(U) with U = I + A_0^{−1} Σ_{i>0} A_i t^{i/m}; the U converge to the identity in the (t^{1/m}, m_K)-adic topology, removing positive powers of t (if M is c-constant start here with m = 1, which preserves |A − I|_1 ≤ c).

The compatibility N A + t dA/dt = q A σ(N) (Kedlaya (17.1.2.1) for σ(t) = t^q), i.e. N − q A σ(N) A^{−1} = −t (dA/dt) A^{−1} (the proof of Lemma 19.3.3 prints the right side without its minus sign, source issue E-RD2-10), then forces N to have only nonpositive powers of t: first modulo q, then modulo q^2, q^3, and so on.
acceptance: The trivial module: m = 1, A = I, N = 0.
Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−1}: A = E(t^{−1}) and N = π_0 t^{−1} (t·d/dt acts by π_0 t^{−1} for ∇v = π_0 t^{−2} v ⊗ dt, the sign of E-RD2-12) already lie in E† ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1}⟧ with m = 1.

nodes.title: Dwork's transfer theorem: the radius of convergence at the centre of a disc is at least the generic radius
nodes.statement: Let K be complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p, β > 0, and M a nonzero finite free differential module (for d/dt) over the ring K⟨t/β⟩ of power series converging on the closed disc |t| ≤ β, or over the ring of functions on the open disc |t| < β. Let R(M ⊗ F_β) be the generic radius of convergence of M at radius β (RD.1/generic-radius). Then for every λ < min{β, R(M ⊗ F_β)}, M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ has a basis of horizontal sections; equivalently the fundamental solution matrix at t = 0 and its inverse converge on the open disc of radius min{β, R(M ⊗ F_β)}: the radius of convergence of M at 0 is at least its generic radius.
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 is needed to form the Taylor series Σ (−t)^i/i! D^i(x).
For the open disc one applies the statement to the restrictions to closed discs of radius β' < β and lets β' → β, using continuity of the generic radius (RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties (d)).
proofSteps: Fix λ < β with λ < ω|D|_{sp,M}^{−1}, ω = p^{−1/(p−1)}, and a supremum norm on M compatible with |·|_λ. Choose ε > 0 with λω^{−1}(|D|_{sp,M} + ε) < 1; there is c > 0 with |D^i(x)| ≤ c(|D|_{sp,M} + ε)^i |x| for all i (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 6.1.8), so the Taylor series y = Σ_i ((−t)^i/i!) D^i(x) converges in M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ since |1/i!| ≤ ω^{−i}.

Differentiating term by term gives D(y) = 0. Applied to a basis of M this yields horizontal sections whose reductions modulo t form a basis, hence a horizontal basis of M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ (a finite differential module over the disc is free and a set of sections whose values at 0 are a basis is a basis: Kedlaya, Proposition 9.1.2).

The spectral norm |D|_{sp,M} is computed after base change to F_β (RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module), which is the definition of the generic radius R(M ⊗ F_β) = ω|D|_{sp}^{−1} (Kedlaya, Definition 9.4.4).
acceptance: Trivial module: R(M ⊗ F_β) = ω|d|_{sp,F_β}^{−1} = β, since |d|_{sp,F_β} = ω/β (Kedlaya, Definition 9.4.4), and the horizontal sections are constants.
The exponential module D(v) = v (horizontal section e^{−t}v): R(M ⊗ F_β) = min{β, ω} and e^{−t} converges exactly on |t| < ω = p^{−1/(p−1)}, so the bound is attained.
Generic-disc form: RD.1/dwork-transfer-generic-disc states the same convergence for discs centred at generic points of the circle |t| = β; this node transfers it to the centre.

sources.match: Dwork's transfer theorem: R(M) ≥ R(M ⊗ F_β) for a nonzero finite differential module over the closed or open disc of radius β, proved by convergence of the Taylor series of horizontal sections.

The generic radius R(V) = ω|D|_{sp,V}^{−1} of a nonzero finite differential module over F_ρ or E; the definition sets R = ρ for the zero module, and the trivial module also has R = ρ because |d|_{sp,F_ρ} = ω/ρ.
The generic-point form: R(E, ρ) ≥ r iff E has a basis of horizontal sections on discs of radius r around points (or a generic point) of the circle |t| = ρ.

nodes.title: A c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-module with c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is trivial (the key lemma of Tsuzuki's theorem)
nodes.statement: Let M be a finite free differential module over E† (resp. over E†_L for a finite separable L/k((t)) whose residue field is separable over k, so that E†_L is a bounded Robba ring over the unramified extension K_L of K in a parameter u) with a unit-root Frobenius structure. If M is c-constant (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module) for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)}, then M is trivial as a differential module: M has a basis of horizontal sections over E† (resp. E†_L). The space H^0(M) of horizontal sections is F-stable, so it is a unit-root Frobenius module over K (resp. K_L) of dimension rank M.
hypotheses: The bound c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is sharp: Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−1}, is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant and not trivial over E† (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module, acceptance).
K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; any Frobenius lift (c-constancy does not depend on it).
proofSteps: Reduce to a standard Frobenius lift σ(t) = t^q (c-constancy is invariant under change of Frobenius, RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module (i)); by RD.2/unit-root-matrix-normal-form choose a c-constant basis on which F and t·d/dt act by A, N with entries in E† ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1}⟧.

The compatibility N A + t dA/dt = q A σ(N) and |A_0| = |A_0^{−1}| = |A|_1 = |A^{−1}|_1 = 1 force N_0 = 0 and |N|_1 ≤ c, so |N|_α ≤ 1 for some α ∈ (0, 1) (A and N then define a module on the region |t^{−1}| ≤ α^{−1}).

Frobenius descent of the system (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, construction in the proof of Lemma 18.2.3): build V with entries in E† ∩ K⟦t^{−1}⟧, |V − I|_1 ≤ c, |V − I|_α ≤ 1, such that A' = V^{−1} A σ(V) and N' = V^{−1} N V + V^{−1} t dV/dt are power series in t^{−p}; substitute t^{−p} ↦ t^{−1} (ψ commutes with the standard σ) and divide N by p: the new pair still satisfies the compatibility, |A'' − I|_1 ≤ c, |N''|_1 ≤ c and |N''|_{α^p} ≤ p.

Log-convexity of ρ ↦ |N''|_ρ in log ρ (Hadamard three circles for Gauss norms of matrices over the ring of the annulus, Kedlaya Proposition 8.2.3(c), a routine property of Laurent series) interpolating between |N''|_1 ≤ c and |N''|_{α^p} ≤ p gives |N''|_β ≤ 1 with log β = (p log c/(log c − log p)) log α; since p log c < log c − log p < 0 this improves α by a fixed factor > 1 in −log, so iterating makes α < p^{−1/(p−1)}.

Then the module M' on the disc |t^{−1}| < α^{−1} with t^{−1} d/dt^{−1} acting by −N has spectral norm of d/dt^{−1} at most α (RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module, Kedlaya Theorem 6.5.3), hence generic radius at radius α^{−1} at least p^{−1/(p−1)}α^{−1} > 1, so by RD.2/dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc its horizontal sections at t^{−1} = 0 converge on a disc of radius > 1 in t^{−1}; restricting to an annulus near |t| = 1 gives a horizontal basis of M (Kedlaya, Lemma 19.3.4).
F-stability of H^0(M): F maps horizontal sections to horizontal sections because ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇.
acceptance: Kedlaya, Proposition 6.11 (arXiv:math/0110124 v4, p. 79) assumes exactly a basis with v_p(A − I) > 1/(p−1), i.e. c-constancy with c < p^{−1/(p−1)}, and concludes that ker ∇ has full rank: this node is a public proof of that step, replacing the citation of Tsuzuki (Amer. J. Math. 120 (1998), Theorem 5.1.1).
Rank one with A = 1 + π^m a, a ∈ O_{E†}, |π|^m < p^{−1/(p−1)}: the horizontal generator exists over E† itself.

sources.match: A finite differential module over E† with unit-root Frobenius structure that is c-constant for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is trivial; proof by Lemma 19.3.3, the Frobenius descent of Lemma 18.2.3, Proposition 8.2.3, Theorem 6.5.3 and Theorem 9.6.1.
Construction of the matrix V with V_i = 0 for p | i solving N_0 V_i − V_i N_0 + i V_i = −(N_W)_i, which makes the system a function of t^p.
Log-convexity and continuity of ρ ↦ |x|_ρ; the Christol-Dwork formula for the spectral norm of a twisted polynomial (an equality, used here as an upper bound).
States the conclusion (kernel of ∇ of full rank and F-stable) under v_p(A − I) > 1/(p − 1), citing Tsuzuki for k algebraically closed and q = p.

nodes.title: Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E† have finite local monodromy, and correspond to representations with finite local monodromy
nodes.statement: (a) (Trivialisation; K complete discretely valued as throughout, any Frobenius lift σ, any k.) Let M be a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† = R^bd. If k is perfect there is a finite separable (Galois) extension L of k((t)) such that M ⊗_{E†} E†_L has a basis of horizontal sections, on which F acts by a matrix in GL_n(K_L); for general k the same holds over E†_{L'} for a nearly finite separable L' (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d)). Consequently M ⊗ R is quasi-constant (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module), and the kernel of ∇ on M ⊗ E†_L is F-stable of rank n over K_L. This is the statement of RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy. (b) (Equivalence; k perfect.) If σ_K is absolute and K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K, then V_0 ↦ D†(V_0 ⊗_{K_0} K) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (c)) is an equivalence of tensor categories from continuous representations of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) with finite local monodromy on finite-dimensional K_0-vector spaces to finite differential modules over E† with a unit-root Frobenius structure; its composite with base change to E is the Fontaine-Katz equivalence (RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence). In particular a continuous K_0-representation has finite local monodromy iff its unit-root module D(V) over E descends to E†.
hypotheses: (a) needs only that σ reduces to the q-power map of k((t)); (b) needs the hypotheses of the Fontaine-Katz equivalence.

For imperfect k a separable L/k((t)) may have inseparable residue extension, so E†_L need not be a bounded Robba ring over a coefficient field; the nearly separable L' of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d) repairs this (Kedlaya, arXiv:math/0110124, proof of Proposition 6.11, last paragraph; Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Section 20.5).
proofSteps: (a), k perfect: choose an étale lattice and, by RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules (c), a finite Galois L with M ⊗ E†_L c-constant for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)}; since k is perfect the residue field of L is separable over k and E†_L is a bounded Robba ring over K_L in a lifted uniformiser u (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c)); RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial gives a horizontal basis, and H^0 is F-stable (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Theorem 19.3.1, p. 321).

(a), general k: by the Lang step the finite separable L exists; replace it by the compositum L' of L with k^{q^{−m}}((t)) for m so large that the residue extension of L' over k^{q^{−m}} is separable (arXiv:math/0110124, proof of Proposition 6.11, last paragraph); c-constancy persists under base change, and the key lemma applies over E†_{L'}, a bounded Robba ring over the m-th Frobenius copy K^{(m)} of K.
Quasi-constancy of M ⊗ R: M ⊗ R^L = (M ⊗ E†_L) ⊗ R^L is spanned by the horizontal basis (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module).

(b) Full faithfulness: D†(V) ⊗ E = D(V) and the Fontaine-Katz equivalence is fully faithful, while every G-equivariant map induces a map of the D† (Kedlaya, proof of Theorem 19.3.1). Essential surjectivity: by (a) M ⊗ E†_L is trivial for a finite Galois L, so the representation V_0(M ⊗ E) is trivial on the inertia subgroup of G_L, i.e. has finite local monodromy, and M = D†(V_0) by Galois descent from E†_L (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (b), (c)).
Converse: if V has finite local monodromy then D†(V) is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† whose base change is D(V).
acceptance: Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}) becomes trivial over the Artin-Schreier extension L: z^p − z = t^{−1} (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example), and corresponds to the character of Gal(L/k((t))) with value ζ_p on z ↦ z + 1 (Kedlaya, Example 19.2.6).
A unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† that is unipotent over R^L is constant over E†_L (Kedlaya, Remark 20.1.5): the generalisation to all slopes is RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement.

Non-example: the rank-one ∇-module E† e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt admits no Frobenius structure (it is not solvable, RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary), so the theorem does not apply to it, and indeed it never becomes trivial over any E†_L.

sources.locator: Theorem 19.3.1 and its proof, pp. 318 and 321
sources.match: Tsuzuki's theorem: for an absolute q-power Frobenius lift with K_0 of residue field F_q and the value group of K, V_0 ↦ D†(V) is an equivalence between representations with finite local monodromy and finite differential modules over E† with unit-root Frobenius structure; the proof chooses L with M ⊗ E†_L c-constant for c < p^{−1/(p−1)} and applies Lemma 19.3.4.

Attribution: rank one to Crew, the general case to Tsuzuki (Amer. J. Math. 1998, Theorem 5.1.1), alternative expositions by Christol and Kedlaya; the c-constancy argument handles the change of Frobenius lift.
The reductions from q = p to q = p^f, from k algebraically closed to general k, and the nearly separable choice of the extension when k is imperfect.
Tsuzuki's theorem in the language of overconvergent unit-root F-isocrystals and potentially unramified local systems; the local model is this equivalence.

nodes.title: ∇-modules that become constant over R^L are semilinear representations of Gal(L/k((t)))
nodes.statement: Let K be complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0, L/k((t)) a finite Galois extension with group G_L = Gal(L/k((t))), R^L the corresponding finite étale extension of the Robba ring (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) and K' the integral closure of K in R^L (its ring of constants). (a) The functor E ↦ H^0(E ⊗_{R_K} R^L) is an equivalence of K-linear tensor categories, compatible with duals, from ∇-modules over R_K that become constant over R^L to finite-dimensional semilinear representations of G_L over K' (G_L acting on K' through its action on R^L); a quasi-inverse is V ↦ (V ⊗_{K'} R^L)^{G_L}. (b) Semilinear representations of a finite group G acting on a field F of characteristic 0 are completely reducible (Maschke), Schur's lemma holds, induction and restriction along a homomorphism G → H are adjoint (Frobenius reciprocity), and every irreducible one is a direct summand of the regular representation F{G}; if G = Gal(F/F_0) acts faithfully, every semilinear representation is trivial (F^n with the coefficient action), since H^1(Gal(F/F_0), GL_n(F)) = 1. (c) Consequently the category M_qc of quasi-constant ∇-modules is closed under direct sums, tensor products, duals, subobjects and quotients (not under extensions), every quasi-constant module is a direct summand of a sum of copies of the pushforward f_*O_X = R^L, and H^0 commutes with duals on M_qc.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (division by |G| in Maschke's averaging); the residue field of L is separable over k (automatic for k perfect), so that R^L ≅ R_{K'} and ker(d on R^L) = K' (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c), RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative); for imperfect k the nearly separable extensions of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d) take the place of L. Kedlaya's overview Lemma 4.3.2 is stated for any formally étale cover.
Right actions as in Kedlaya's overview, Convention 4.2.1; the twisted group algebra F{G} has c{g}·d{h} = c d^{g^{−1}} {gh}.
proofSteps: (b) Maschke: average a projector over G (Kedlaya overview Lemma 4.2.3); Schur: kernels and images are subrepresentations (Lemma 4.2.4); Frobenius reciprocity: induction V ⊗_{F{G}} F{H} is left adjoint to restriction (Lemma 4.2.7); Corollary 4.2.9 by reciprocity applied to the trivial group; triviality for G = Gal(F/F_0) by Hilbert-Noether descent (Remark 4.2.5; Tau Ceti's TauCeti.GaloisDescent.span_invariants_eq_top and liftBaseChange_injective_of_invariant).

(a) Full faithfulness: H^0(E ⊗ R^L)^∨ ⊗ H^0(F ⊗ R^L) ≅ H^0((E^∨ ⊗ F) ⊗ R^L) by dimension count and injectivity, and G_L-invariant horizontal sections of E^∨ ⊗ F over R^L are horizontal sections over R_K (RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative: ker d on R^L is K'); essential surjectivity: H^0(R^L) is the regular representation of G_L over K', so an irreducible V is the image of a G_L-equivariant projector on H^0(R^L), which comes from a projector of the ∇-module R^L over R_K (overview Lemma 4.3.2).
(c) follows from (a) and (b) as in overview Definition 4.3.1 and the proof of Proposition 4.4.3.
acceptance: E = (R_K, d): H^0(E ⊗ R^L) = K' with the coefficient action.
The pushforward of R^L to R_K corresponds to the regular representation K'{G_L}.

Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}) becomes constant over the Artin-Schreier extension L (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example) and corresponds to a nontrivial character of Gal(L/k((t))) ≅ Z/p (K' = K when k is algebraically closed in L).
Non-example to closure under extensions: the unipotent module with ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ dt/t (SFR Example 7.2.6) is an extension of two constant modules but is not quasi-constant (its monodromy N ≠ 0).

sources.match: Maschke, Schur, Frobenius reciprocity and the regular representation for semilinear representations of finite groups, and triviality of semilinear Galois representations by vanishing of H^1(G, GL_n).
Quasi-constant ∇-modules and the equivalence E ↦ H^0(E, X) with semilinear representations of Gal(R/k((t))) over the constants K'.
After enlarging K, H^0(M ⊗ R^L) is a linear representation of the finite group G_{L/k((t))}, defined over a finite extension of Q_p.

nodes.title: Matsuda's decomposition of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules as ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k, and M_qu the category of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules over R_K (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module). (a) (Dualizability) For E ∈ M_qu, H^0(E) and H^1(E) = coker(∇) are finite-dimensional and the residue pairing H^0(E^∨) × H^1(E) → H^1(E^∨ ⊗ E) → H^1(R_K) ≅ K (residue of Σ c_i t^i dt ↦ c_{−1}) is perfect. (b) For P quasi-constant and U unipotent, H^0(P) ⊗_K H^0(U) → H^0(P ⊗ U) is an isomorphism; a nonzero indecomposable unipotent U has dim H^0(U) = dim H^1(U) = 1. (c) If E_j is F_j-typical (a successive extension of copies of an irreducible F_j) for j = 1, 2 with F_1 ≇ F_2, then Ext^i(E_1, E_2) = 0 for i = 0, 1. (d) Every E ∈ M_qu has a decomposition E ≅ ⊕_i F_i ⊗ U_i, unique up to reordering and isomorphism, with F_i quasi-constant irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic and U_i unipotent; in particular every indecomposable quasi-unipotent module is F ⊗ U with F quasi-constant irreducible and U unipotent indecomposable.
hypotheses: Quasi-unipotent means a filtration with quasi-constant successive quotients; M_qu is closed under direct sums, tensor products, duals, subquotients and extensions (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.6.1).

K discretely valued and k perfect, as in Kedlaya's book (Proposition 20.4.2, whose Section 20.5 explains how to remove perfectness). Kedlaya's overview states (a)-(d) under its Convention 4.0.8 (K complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0), but the proof of its Proposition 4.4.3 enlarges K until the cover R^L becomes a Robba ring over a finite extension of K, which overview Remark 3.5.7 provides when the residue extension of L over k is separable, in particular for k perfect. Every consumer in this packet assumes k perfect; for imperfect k the nearly separable extensions of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d) are the route of the book's Section 20.5.

The perfect residue pairing for (φ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Proposition 20.4.2; planned as RD.1/robba-residue-duality by the RD.1 continuation) is (a) combined with the p-adic local monodromy theorem RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement; (a) is the public proof that node's gap G5 asks for.
proofSteps: (a) Dualizability is stable under direct sums and extensions (snake lemma on 0 → H^0(E_2^∨) → H^0(E^∨) → H^0(E_1^∨) against the dual H^1 sequence; overview Remark 4.4.2), so it suffices to treat E quasi-constant; by Q1 (c) E is a summand of copies of f_*O_X with H^i(f_*O_X) = H^i(R^L), and after a finite Galois extension of K (which commutes with H^0 and H^1) R^L is a Robba ring with H^0 = H^1 = K' by RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative (overview Proposition 4.4.3).

(b) Induction on rank U using 0 → O → U → U_1 → 0, the five lemma and (a) for the H^1 term (overview Lemma 4.5.6); the indecomposable case is the Jordan-block statement for nilpotent matrices through RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue (overview Lemma 4.5.5).
(c) Ext^i(E_1, E_2) = H^i(E_1^∨ ⊗ E_2); by (a) reduce to i = 0, then induction on rank and Schur's lemma (overview Lemma 4.6.4).

(d) Existence of the decomposition into F-typical pieces by induction on rank with (c) (overview Proposition 4.6.5); an F-typical E is F ⊗ U: if 0 → E_1 → E → F → 0 with E_1 ≅ F ⊗ U_1, then Ext^1(F, E_1) = H^0(F^∨ ⊗ F)^∨ ⊗ Ext^1(O, U_1) by (a), (b), and after an automorphism of F the extension class comes from an extension of O by U_1 (overview Theorem 4.6.6; Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Corollary 20.4.3).
acceptance: E = R_K: H^0 = H^1 = K and the pairing is the residue pairing K × K → K, (a, b) ↦ ab.
The unipotent module U_2 with ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ dt/t: dim H^0 = dim H^1 = 1 (ker and coker of the nilpotent Jordan block, RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue).

For F the rank-one module of a nontrivial Artin-Schreier character and U_2 as above, F ⊗ U_2 is indecomposable, quasi-unipotent and neither quasi-constant nor unipotent; H^0(F ⊗ U_2) = H^0(F) ⊗ H^0(U_2) = 0.

sources.match: The local duality pairing H^0(E^∨) × H^1(E) → K and its perfectness for quasi-constant modules and their successive extensions.

sources.locator: Lemmas 4.5.5 and 4.5.6, Definition 4.6.1, Definition 4.6.3, Lemma 4.6.4, Proposition 4.6.5, Theorem 4.6.6, pp. 23-26
sources.match: Indecomposable unipotent modules, the tensor formula for H^0, vanishing of Ext between typical modules, the typical decomposition, and Matsuda's decomposition E ≅ ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i.
Galois descent of H^0 and H^1, the perfect pairing for quasi-unipotent modules over the Robba ring (k perfect), and Matsuda's decomposition of indecomposable quasi-unipotent modules.

nodes.title: Highest breaks under unipotent twists, tame covers and Artin-Schreier covers
nodes.statement: Let K be complete of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p, and use the highest break of RD.1/highest-break (E has highest break ≤ β iff R(E, ρ) ≥ ρ^{β+1} for ρ close to 1). (a) A unipotent E has highest break 0. (b) If E has highest break ≤ α and F has highest break β > α, then E ⊗ F has highest break β. (c) Let f be the cover t ↦ t^n with p ∤ n. Then E has highest break ≥ β (resp. ≤ β) iff f^*E has highest break ≥ nβ (resp. ≤ nβ), iff f_*E has highest break ≥ β/n (resp. ≤ β/n). (d) Let a ∈ k^×, p ∤ n, and f the finite étale cover whose reduction is the Artin-Schreier extension u^p − u = a t^{−n}. If E has no trivial submodule and f^*E is constant, then E has highest break n; the same holds for the reduction u^p − u = P(t^{−1}) with P a polynomial of degree n prime to p. (e) With f as in (d) and β ≥ n, E has highest break ≤ β iff f^*E has highest break ≤ βp − n(p − 1).
hypotheses: In (d) and (e) one may enlarge K (by π_0 with π_0^{p−1} = −p and an n-th root of a); breaks do not change under finite extensions of K (RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties (f)).
βp − n(p − 1) is the upper numbering of the break β over the Artin-Schreier extension with break n (Herbrand function, Kedlaya overview Example 2.1.10).
proofSteps: Generic discs: for p ∤ n the map z ↦ z^n identifies |t − t_ρ^{1/n}| < rρ^{1/n} with |t − t_ρ| < rρ; for z ↦ z^p it identifies |t − t_ρ^{1/p}| < rpρ^{1/p} with |t − t_ρ| < rρ when r ≤ p^{−p/(p−1)}; for the Artin-Schreier cover (1 + π_0 u)^p = 1 + pπ_0 t^{−1} it identifies |u^{−1} − u_ρ^{−1}| < rρ^{(2−p)/p} with |t − t_ρ| < rρ (Kedlaya overview Lemmas 5.3.1-5.3.3); with RD.1/dwork-transfer-generic-disc this translates convergence of horizontal sections around generic points.

(a) A unipotent basis gives ∇ with nilpotent matrix in dt/t and log(t/t_ρ) converges on |t − t_ρ| < ρ (overview Lemma 5.4.4, using RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue). (b) Horizontal sections of E ⊗ F are products of those of E and F (Lemma 5.4.5). (c) Disc comparison for z ↦ z^n (Lemma 5.4.6).

(d) After enlarging K, E is a nontrivial rank-one summand of f_*f^*O, presented with b ∈ O_K lifting −a (source issue E-RD2-9) and generated by v = (1 + π_0 u)^i for some 1 ≤ i ≤ p − 1, with ∇v = −iπ_0 n b t^{−n−1}(1 + pπ_0 b t^{−n})^{−1} v ⊗ dt (the overview omits the factor i, source issue E-RD2-11), isomorphic near the boundary to ∇w = −iπ_0 n b t^{−n−1} w ⊗ dt, whose horizontal section exp(−iπ_0 b(t^{−n} − t_ρ^{−n})) converges exactly on |t − t_ρ| < ρ^{n+1} because |i| = 1 (Lemma 5.4.7; compare RD.1/dwork-exponential-module for n = 1); the polynomial case by induction on degree with (b) (Lemma 5.4.9).

(e) The case n = 1 from the Artin-Schreier disc comparison; general n by composing with t ↦ t^n and (c), using that E is a direct summand of g^*g_*E and of f_*f^*E through trace and adjunction maps (Lemma 5.4.8).
acceptance: The trivial module has highest break 0, and so does the unipotent module of SFR Example 7.2.6.
Dwork's module M_f with f = t^{−1} has highest break 1 (n = 1 in (d)); with f = t^{−n}, p ∤ n, highest break n.
Tame: the Kummer module ∇v = (1/2) v ⊗ dt/t (p odd) becomes trivial under t ↦ t^2 and has highest break 0 = 2·0, consistent with (c).
(e) with n = 1, β = 1: the Artin-Schreier pullback of M_{t^{−1}} is trivial, of break 0 ≤ 1·p − 1·(p − 1) = 1.

sources.match: How discs around generic points transform under z ↦ z^n (p ∤ n), z ↦ z^p and the Artin-Schreier cover.

Highest breaks via R(E, ρ) ≥ ρ^{β+1}; unipotent modules have break 0; tensor products; tame covers multiply breaks by n; Artin-Schreier rank-one modules have break n; breaks over an Artin-Schreier cover become βp − n(p − 1).
An Artin-Schreier extension u^p − u = P(t^{−1}) with deg P = d prime to p has the single break d, and the Herbrand function is m for m ≤ d and d + (m − d)/p beyond.

nodes.title: The highest break of a quasi-unipotent ∇-module equals the highest ramification break of its monodromy representation
nodes.statement: Suppose k is perfect. Let E be a quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_K and τ its monodromy representation restricted to the inertia group I of Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) (RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence; I acts through a finite quotient). If the highest upper-numbering break of τ (in the sense of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor, with G^0 = I and G^{0+} = P the wild inertia) is β, then E has highest break β (RD.1/highest-break; E is solvable at 1 by RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent, so its highest break is defined); in particular E has highest break 0 iff P acts trivially, i.e. iff τ is tame.
hypotheses: k perfect, so the ramification filtration of Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) is the classical one (Serre's numbering, G_0 inertia, G_1 wild); the finite-residue-field case is supplied by Tau Ceti through R01.3 and the perfect infinite case rests on R01.3's recorded ramification gap.
β ∈ Q_{≥0}; for nonabelian images β need not be an integer, and β ∈ (0, 1) occurs after tame base change (Kedlaya overview Lemma 5.4.6).
proofSteps: Enlarge k to an algebraic closure, i.e. replace K by the completion of its maximal unramified extension: the inertia group with its upper ramification filtration does not change, so neither do the Galois breaks (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-unramified-base-change records the consequence for the conductor and the Swan conductor), and generic radii and differential breaks are unchanged as well (RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties (f)). By RD.2/highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback (c) pass to a tame cover so that the image H of τ is a p-group; by RD.2/matsuda-decomposition and parts (a), (b) of that lemma reduce to E quasi-constant and irreducible (Kedlaya overview, proof of Theorem 5.4.10).

Induct on |H| and then on the lowest upper break i of H, an integer by Hasse-Arf for the abelian quotient (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-of-a-character). Base case |H| = p: Lemma 5.4.9 = part (d) of RD.2/highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback with the break of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/artin-schreier-break.

Inductive step: choose a maximal subgroup N ⊇ H^i, normal of index p, fixing an Artin-Schreier extension u^p − u = Σ_{j≤i} c_j t^{−j} (p ∤ j); over it either E becomes constant (break i by part (d)) or the highest break of τ becomes βp − (p − 1)i (Herbrand function, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/upper-numbering-of-an-open-subgroup) with a smaller lowest break, so the induction hypothesis gives the break of f^*E and part (e) gives β for E; β = i is excluded because H would then be elementary abelian, hence of order p.
acceptance: Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−n} (p ∤ n): its monodromy is the Artin-Schreier character of u^p − u = t^{−n}, of upper break n, and its highest break is n.
A tamely ramified character of order m prime to p (Kummer module ∇v = (a/m) v ⊗ dt/t): break 0 on both sides.
A representation with highest upper break 1/2 (Artin-Schreier over t^{1/2}, p odd): the module has highest break 1/2 (part (c) with n = 2).

sources.match: For k perfect, a quasi-unipotent E whose monodromy representation has highest break β has highest break β; proof by reduction to p-group images and double induction using Lemmas 5.4.4-5.4.9.
Attribution: for K discretely valued this is Matsuda's Corollary 8.8; related results of Tsuzuki (Theorem 7.2.2) and Crew (Theorem 5.4), and André's Tannakian Complement 7.1.2.
Hasse-Arf: breaks of abelian extensions are integers, used for the lowest break of the p-group image.

nodes.title: Break decompositions match ramification: the differential Swan conductor equals the Swan conductor of the monodromy
nodes.statement: Suppose k is perfect and E is a quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_K (for instance one admitting a Frobenius structure, by RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement), with monodromy representation V restricted to inertia. (a) The monodromy equivalence (RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence) carries the break decomposition E = ⊕_b E_b of RD.1/break-decomposition to the break decomposition V = ⊕_λ V(λ) of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor: E_b corresponds to V(b). (b) Hence the break multisets agree and the differential Swan conductor (irregularity) equals the Galois Swan conductor: Swan(E) (RD.1/differential-swan-conductor) = Sw(V). In particular Swan(E) is a nonnegative integer (Hasse-Arf, R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality), which recovers RD.1/swan-conductor-integrality for quasi-unipotent modules. (c) For a representation V of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) with finite local monodromy and D†(V) as in RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module, for ρ < 1 close to 1 the intrinsic generic radius is IR(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = ρ^{b} (equivalently R(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = ρ^{b+1}) where b is the highest upper break of V|_I, and the intrinsic subsidiary radii are ρ^{b_1}, …, ρ^{b_n}, the b_j being the highest breaks of the constituents V_j of V|_I counted with multiplicity dim V_j.
hypotheses: k perfect (as in R01.3, tier (P) of which rests on its recorded ramification gap; tier (F) for finite k is supplied by Tau Ceti).

Normalisation: breaks are Serre's upper numbering (G^0 = inertia, G^{0+} = wild inertia), and IR = R/ρ is the intrinsic radius of RD.1/generic-radius; Kedlaya's book (Theorem 19.4.1, Corollary 19.4.2) prints R = ρ^b with b = max{i ≥ 1 : G^i ⊄ ker τ}, which must be read with IR in place of R and with b allowed in [0, ∞) (source issue recorded in this packet).
proofSteps: (a) E is solvable at 1 (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent), so its break decomposition and Swan conductor are defined. By RD.2/matsuda-decomposition and the Galois-theoretic break decomposition, it suffices to show that an indecomposable E with monodromy of uniform break λ has uniform break λ; apply RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem to E and to all its subquotients, which pins down the generic radii of every Jordan-Hölder constituent (Kedlaya overview Corollary 5.4.11 and Remark 5.4.12).
(b) Sum the breaks with multiplicities on both sides; Sw(V) = Σ_λ λ dim V(λ) by definition (R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor) and Swan(E) = Σ_b b·rank E_b (RD.1/differential-swan-conductor).
(c) D†(V) ⊗ R is quasi-constant with monodromy V|_I (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (e)); apply (a) and the definition of intrinsic subsidiary radii (RD.1/generic-radius).
acceptance: Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}}: Swan = 1 = Sw of the Artin-Schreier character (R01.3/artin-schreier-swan-conductor: Sw = m for u^p − u = u_0 with v(u_0) = −m); IR = ρ, R = ρ^2 near the boundary (RD.1/dwork-exponential-module).
A tamely ramified or unramified V: all breaks 0, Swan(E) = Sw(V) = 0, IR(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = 1.

Integrality: for the induced representation from a ramified Artin-Schreier extension of break 1 over the tame extension t^{1/2} (p odd), V is two-dimensional with upper break 1/2 and Sw(V) = 2·(1/2) = 1, an integer, matching the differential Swan conductor of the rank-two module.

sources.match: The monodromy equivalence commutes with break decompositions; attribution to Matsuda (Corollary 8.8), Tsuzuki (Theorem 7.2.2) and Crew (Theorem 5.4).

For finite local monodromy, the generic radius of D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ near 1 is computed from the highest upper break, the subsidiary radii from the constituents, and integrality of the product of subsidiary radii is the Hasse-Arf theorem (stated without proof; the radius must be read as the intrinsic radius).

The isomorphism G^{>0} ≅ P identifies the p-adic slope filtration with the upper ramification filtration (Matsuda-Tsuzuki), proved by comparing Swan conductor and p-adic irregularity on K_0(Rep I) via Artin induction and the rank-one computation.

nodes.title: Over algebraic coefficients every quasi-unipotent ∇-module carries a Frobenius structure at a finite level
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. Let K_0 = W(k)[1/p] ⊆ K. Say that an object M of MC(R_{K̄}/K̄) admits a Frobenius structure at finite level if there are a finite extension K_1 of K_0 inside K̄, a Frobenius lift σ_1 of K_1 (a continuous endomorphism lifting x ↦ x^{p^h} on the residue field, for some h ≥ 1), a (σ_1,∇)-module M_1 over R_{K_1} for the standard lift t ↦ t^{p^h} (RD.1/frobenius-differential-module), and an isomorphism M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} ≅ M of ∇-modules. (a) Every quasi-constant ∇-module M over some R_{K'} (K'/K finite) becomes, over R_{K̄}, isomorphic to M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} with M_1 a (σ_1,∇)-module over R_{K_1}, where F is a finite extension of Q_p inside K̄, k' the compositum of k and the residue field F_{p^f} of F, K_1 = F·W(k')[1/p] and σ_1 = id_F ⊗ φ_W^h (φ_W the Witt-vector Frobenius, f | h). (b) Every unipotent ∇-module over R_{K̄} is the base change of a module over R_{K_0} in Jordan form, which carries a Frobenius structure for every Frobenius lift of K_0. (c) Hence every quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_{K̄} admits a Frobenius structure at finite level; in the notation of RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants, MC^qu(R_{K̄}/K̄) ⊆ MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄). The existence of such a structure does not depend on the choice of the lift t ↦ t^{p^h} (RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures).
hypotheses: k perfect, so K is a finite totally ramified extension of K_0 = W(k)[1/p] and K̄ is also an algebraic closure of K_0. With F^ur the maximal unramified subextension of F/Q_p, F^ur ⊆ W(k')[1/p], and F·W(k')[1/p] = F ⊗_{F^ur} W(k')[1/p] is a field (F/F^ur totally ramified, W(k')[1/p]/F^ur unramified); id_F ⊗ φ_W^h is well defined because φ_W^h fixes F^ur when f | h.

Working at a finite, discretely valued level is what makes the p-adic local monodromy theorem applicable; André's definition (§3.4) asks instead for an isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M over R_{K̄} for an automorphism σ of K̄, which contains the present notion (σ_1 extends to such a σ).
proofSteps: (a) After a finite extension of the constants, H^0(M ⊗ R^L) is a linear representation of the finite group Gal(L/k((t))) (RD.2/quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations), which can be defined over a finite extension F of Q_p inside K̄ with a stable O_F-lattice T (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 20.1.3, p. 327). The equivalence of RD.2/quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations over K_1 = F·W(k')[1/p] produces M_1 with M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} ≅ M ⊗ R_{K̄}; declaring T fixed defines a Frobenius structure for σ_1 = id_F ⊗ φ_W^h on M_1 ⊗ R^L, which commutes with the Galois action and descends to M_1.

(b) A unipotent M is V ⊗ R with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N nilpotent (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); after a change of basis N is a Jordan matrix with entries 0 and 1, so M is defined over R_{K_0}; the pull-back along t ↦ t^{q} (q = p^h) has residue qN, conjugate to N by a diagonal matrix with entries powers of q, which gives the Frobenius structure.

(c) By RD.2/matsuda-decomposition a quasi-unipotent M is ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i; take K_1 the compositum of the fields of (a) for the F_i and h a common multiple of the orders (a structure of order h induces one of every multiple order by iteration); tensor products and direct sums of the structures of (a) and (b) give one on M at the level R_{K_1}.
acceptance: (R_{K_0}, d) with the standard lift: a Frobenius structure for every h.

The Kummer module ∇v = (1/m) v ⊗ dt/t with p ∤ m: quasi-constant (trivial after t ↦ t^{1/m}); for h with m | p^h − 1, the map 1 ⊗ v ↦ t^{(p^h − 1)/m}·v is a horizontal isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M (the pulled-back connection is (p^h/m) dt/t), a Frobenius structure of order h already over R_{Q_p}.

Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}} is defined over R_{Q_p(π_0)} (π_0^{p−1} = −p) with ∇v = π_0 t^{−2} v ⊗ dt and the Frobenius structure exp(π_0(t^{−1} − t^{−p})) for σ_1 = id; its dual E_π of RD.1/dwork-exponential-module has ∇w = −π_0 t^{−2} w ⊗ dt and Frobenius structure exp(π_0(t^{−p} − t^{−1})) (source issue E-RD2-12).

sources.match: A quasi-unipotent module is solvable at 1: after enlarging K, the horizontal sections over R^L form a representation of a finite group with a stable lattice over a finite extension of Q_p, and declaring it fixed gives a Frobenius structure for an absolute Frobenius lift fixing that field.
Defines Frobenius structures of order h on objects of MC(R_K̄/K̄) via φ_h (z ↦ z^{p^h}, σ lifting the p^h-power map) and MCF as the objects admitting one, noting that only existence matters.
For k algebraically closed the monodromy-representation description of quasi-unipotent modules is essentially André's Théorème 7.1.1, i.e. MCF is described by all permissible representations.

nodes.title: The Tannakian categories MC(R_K̄/K̄) ⊇ MCS ⊇ MCF of differential modules over the Robba ring with algebraic constants
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. (a) MC(R_{K̄}/K̄) is the category of finitely presented R_{K̄}-modules with a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1 (Leibniz rule for d); every object is finite free and is the base change of an object over R_{K'} for some finite K'/K, and Hom-spaces are the colimits of those over the R_{K'}; with ⊗ over R_{K̄}, duals and the unit (R_{K̄}, d) it is a K̄-linear abelian rigid tensor category with End(1) = K̄. (b) Full subcategories: MC^uni of unipotent objects (successive extensions of the unit), MC^qu of quasi-unipotent objects, MCS of objects solvable at 1 (RD.1/solvable-at-boundary), and MCF of objects admitting a Frobenius structure at finite level (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures); only the existence of a Frobenius structure is recorded, not the structure itself. (c) MC^uni ≃ Vec^nil_{K̄} (finite-dimensional K̄-spaces with a nilpotent endomorphism) via (V, N) ↦ (V ⊗_{K̄} R_{K̄}, d + N dt/t), so the Tannakian group of MC^uni is G_a. (d) MCF = MC^qu ⊆ MCS, and MCF is a Tannakian subcategory stable under subquotients and extensions. (e) The logarithmic fibre functor ω : MCF → Vec_{K̄}, ω(M) = colim_L H^0(M ⊗ R^L_{K̄,log}) (L finite separable over k̄((t)), R^L_log = R^L[log t] as in RD.2/log-robba-ring), is an exact faithful tensor functor, and ω(M) carries commuting actions of I (through the Galois action on R^L_log, fixing log t) and of G_a (c ∈ K̄ acting by log t ↦ log t + c), with dim ω(M) = rank M.
hypotheses: K discretely valued with perfect residue field; the colimit over K' ⊆ K̄ is taken inside a fixed algebraic closure, so R_{K̄} is an integral domain (K is algebraically closed in R_K).

(d) uses the p-adic local monodromy theorem (RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) at the finite level K_1 for MCF ⊆ MC^qu; André obtains the Tannakian property from Christol-Mebkhout's theory instead. With André's definition (an isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M over R_{K̄} for an automorphism σ of K̄) the category contains this one, and coincides with it by André's Théorème 7.1.1, which shows that all its objects are quasi-unipotent; that comparison is cited, not planned.
proofSteps: (a) Finitely presented modules with connection over a Robba ring are free (RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free); a presentation involves finitely many coefficients, hence descends to some R_{K'}; rigidity and End(1) = ker(d on R_{K̄}) = K̄ (RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative).
(c) Base change of RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue to K̄ (André §3.4; Xu-Zhu §2.9.1, p. 23); Vec^nil_{K̄} is the category of representations of G_a (c acting by exp(cN)).

(d) MCF ⊆ MC^qu by the p-adic local monodromy theorem applied to M_1 over R_{K_1} (K_1 discretely valued with Frobenius lift σ_1; quasi-unipotence is preserved by base change to R_{K̄}); MC^qu ⊆ MCF by RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures; MC^qu is stable under subquotients, tensor products, duals and extensions (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.6.1); MCF ⊆ MCS by Dwork's argument (RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability).

(e) By the logarithmic form of the local monodromy theorem (RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy) and RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module, for L large H^0(M ⊗ R^L_log) has dimension rank M over the constants and the transition maps are isomorphisms after extending constants; exactness and the tensor property follow from the comparison isomorphism H^0(M ⊗ R^L_log) ⊗ R^L_log ≅ M ⊗ R^L_log.
acceptance: The unit (R_{K̄}, d) ↦ ω = K̄ with trivial I × G_a action.
U_2 = (K̄², N = [[0,1],[0,0]]) ↦ ω(U_2) = K̄² with G_a acting by [[1,c],[0,1]] (up to the sign convention for N) and I trivially.
Non-example for MCS ⊆ MCF: the rank-one module ∇e = λ e ⊗ dt/t with λ ∈ Z_p not in Q (Kedlaya, Example 9.5.2: solvable at 1) is in MCS but not quasi-unipotent, hence not in MCF.
Non-example for MC ⊆ MCS: ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not solvable (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

nodes.title: Solutions of a unipotent ∇-module on the open unit disc: Sol(M) ≅ (coker N)^∨
nodes.statement: Let K{x} be the ring of analytic functions on the open unit disc |x| < 1 (Σ a_n x^n with |a_n| ρ^n → 0 for every ρ < 1), with the logarithmic derivation d : K{x} → Ω^1_{K{x}}(log) = K{x}·dx/x, f ↦ x f'(x) dx/x. Let M be a unipotent ∇-module over R_K corresponding to (V, N) (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue), extended to the log-∇-module M_log = V ⊗ K{x} with ∇(v) = Nv ⊗ dx/x on the disc. Then the solution space Sol(M) := Hom_{K{x}}((M_log, ∇), (K{x}, d))^{∇=0} of horizontal homomorphisms is canonically isomorphic to (coker N)^∨ = ker(N^∨ on V^∨): every horizontal φ is constant, φ(v) = λ(v) with λ ∈ V^∨ and λ∘N = 0. If ∇ is defined by a differential operator D (M = K{x}[∂]/K{x}[∂]D), Sol(M) is the space of solutions of D in K{x}. If M carries a Frobenius structure extending to the disc, Sol(M) and coker N are (φ, N)-modules with N φ = q φ N, compatibly with the duality.
hypotheses: K complete of characteristic 0; the residue N is nilpotent (unipotent M).

Xu-Zhu (2.9.2.2) print a canonical isomorphism Coker(N) ≅ Sol(M); the solution space is the dual of the cokernel (source issue recorded in this packet). Dimensions agree, which is all that their subsequent argument (proof of Proposition 5.1.3) requires.
proofSteps: Write φ(v) = Σ_{n≥0} φ_n(v) x^n with φ_n ∈ V^∨. Horizontality φ(Nv) = x d/dx φ(v) gives φ_n∘N = n φ_n for every n; for n ≥ 1, N − n is invertible (N nilpotent), so φ_n = 0, and for n = 0 the condition is φ_0∘N = 0 (Xu-Zhu §2.9.2, p. 24, in corrected form).
Conversely each λ ∈ V^∨ with λ∘N = 0 defines a horizontal homomorphism; so Sol(M) ≅ (V/NV)^∨.
For M = K{x}[∂]/K{x}[∂]D, a horizontal homomorphism is determined by the image y of the class of 1, which satisfies D(y) = 0.

Frobenius: a Frobenius structure extending to the disc is constant on a horizontal basis (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Proposition 17.5.1), giving φ on V with N φ = q φ N (Remark 17.1.2); it induces the dual structure on Sol(M).
acceptance: M = (R_K, d): V = K, N = 0, Sol(M) = K (the constant functions).
M = U_2 (N e_2 = e_1, N e_1 = 0): coker N is spanned by the class of e_2, and Sol(M) is spanned by the functional e_1^∨ ↦ 0, e_2^∨-dual: λ(e_1) = 0, λ(e_2) = 1; one-dimensional.
The operator D = (x d/dx)^2: M ≅ U_2 and its solutions in K{x} are the constants (log x is not in K{x}), one-dimensional = dim coker N.
