nodes.title: André's local monodromy theorem: the Tannakian group of MCF(R_K̄/K̄) is I × G_a, with wild part P
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. (a) The logarithmic fibre functor ω of RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants (e) is an equivalence of K̄-linear rigid tensor categories from MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄) to the category Rep_{K̄}(I × G_a) of finite-dimensional K̄-vector spaces with a linear action of I whose kernel is open and a commuting nilpotent endomorphism N (c ∈ G_a acting by exp(cN)); equivalently, to the finite-dimensional comodules over the commutative Hopf algebra H = C^lc(I, K̄) ⊗ K̄[x] of locally constant functions on I tensored with the coordinate ring of G_a. (b) Consequently the Tannakian group Aut^⊗(ω) is I × G_a: for every commutative K̄-algebra A, Aut^⊗(ω ⊗ A) ≅ Hom_{K̄-alg}(H, A), naturally in A. (c) Under (a), an object has all p-adic slopes zero (highest break 0, RD.1/highest-break) iff P acts trivially on ω(M); more precisely the break filtration of MCF by p-adic slopes corresponds to the upper ramification filtration of P, so that 𝒢^{>0} ≅ P, and the irregularity of M equals the Swan conductor of ω(M)|_I. (d) The tame factor: for M unipotent with (V, N) as in RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue, ω(M) = V with G_a acting through N (up to sign), H^0(M) = ker N = ω(M)^{I × G_a} and H^1(M) = coker N = the G_a-coinvariants of ω(M); the solution space of RD.2/unipotent-solutions-and-residues is the dual (coker N)^∨. (e) Every indecomposable object is isomorphic to F ⊗ U_m with F coming from an irreducible representation of I with finite image and U_m the m-dimensional indecomposable unipotent object; an object M with End(M)^{𝒢^{>0}} = K̄ (completely irreducible) is absolutely irreducible of rank a power of p.
hypotheses: k perfect and K discretely valued (André, §7.1). Over K itself (not K̄) the same functor gives the semilinear form RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence.

Tannakian reconstruction is used only in the form of Tau Ceti's comodule reconstruction (points of a commutative Hopf algebra = tensor automorphisms of scalar extension on its finite-dimensional comodules); no general reconstruction of a neutral Tannakian category is needed, because (a) identifies MCF with a comodule category explicitly.
proofSteps: (a) Over K̄ the coefficient Galois action is trivial (residue field k̄ algebraically closed), so the monodromy representation of RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence becomes a linear permissible representation of I × G_a, and that theorem (quasi-unipotent modules ≃ permissible representations, Kedlaya overview Theorem 4.7.6) applied over each R_{K'} and passed to the colimit (for M defined over R_{K'}, restrict its semilinear monodromy representation to I × G_a, which acts K'^unr-linearly because I fixes the coefficients, and extend scalars to K̄; objects, morphisms and representations with open kernel are all defined at some finite level, so full faithfulness and essential surjectivity pass to the colimit) gives the equivalence on MC^qu = MCF (RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants (d)); tensor compatibility from the comparison isomorphism of RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module.

Comodules over H: H is a commutative Hopf algebra over K̄, built in this node because Tau Ceti's reconstruction takes the Hopf algebra as given: C^lc(I, K̄) is the colimit, over open normal subgroups U of I, of the function algebras K̄^{I/U} of the finite groups I/U with comultiplication dual to the group law, and K̄[x] has x ↦ x ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ x. A finite-dimensional comodule over C^lc(I, K̄) is a representation of I with open kernel (its coefficients lie in some K̄^{I/U}), and one over K̄[x] is a nilpotent endomorphism (characteristic 0), so Comod_fd(H) = Rep_{K̄}(I × G_a).

(b) Tau Ceti's reconstruction TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor (and its pointwise form TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv) identifies Hom_{K̄-alg}(H, A) with the tensor automorphisms of scalar extension to A on finite-dimensional H-comodules; transport along (a).

(c) RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem and RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor: the break decomposition corresponds to the Galois break decomposition, and break 0 means P acts trivially (G^{0+} = P); this is André's Complément 7.1.2.
(d) RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue (H^0 = ker N, H^1 = coker N) and the action log t ↦ log t + c on horizontal log-sections (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.7.5).

(e) Indecomposable representations of I × G_a with I acting through a finite group are W ⊗ (Jordan block) with W irreducible (André Corollaire 7.1.6; equivalently RD.2/matsuda-decomposition); for completely irreducible M, End of the restriction to 𝒢^{>0} = P is K̄, so M|_P is irreducible and P is a pro-p group acting through a finite p-group, whose irreducible representations have p-power dimension (André Corollaire 7.1.8).
acceptance: The unit object ↦ the trivial representation; U_m ↦ the m-dimensional Jordan block of G_a.
Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}} ↦ the Artin-Schreier character of I of conductor 2 (Swan conductor 1), nontrivial on P.
Kummer module ∇v = (1/m) v ⊗ dt/t (p ∤ m) ↦ a tame character of I of order m (trivial on P), irregularity 0.
André Corollaire 7.1.3: if k is finite, the isomorphism classes of objects of MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄) form a countable set, because I has countably many open subgroups.

sources.locator: Théorème 7.1.1, Complément 7.1.2 and proof, Corollaires 7.1.3, 7.1.5-7.1.8, pp. 24-26
sources.match: MCF(R_K̄/K̄) has Tannakian group I × G_a with 𝒢^{>0} = P; the p-adic slope filtration matches the upper ramification filtration (Matsuda-Tsuzuki); countability for finite k; log solutions after a finite étale extension; indecomposables M ⊗ U_m; completely irreducible objects have p-power rank.
Restates André's isomorphisms 𝒢 ≅ I × G_a and 𝒢^{>0} ≅ P, the quasi-unipotence of MCF, finiteness of the action of P, and irregularity = Swan conductor of the I-representation on a fibre.
The monodromy representation is an equivalence from quasi-unipotent ∇-modules to permissible representations of G_log; for k algebraically closed this is essentially André's Théorème 7.1.1.

nodes.title: The p-adic local monodromy theorem over every finite étale extension R^L of the Robba ring, and for rings presented as such
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of characteristic 0, σ a Frobenius lift on R_K, L/k((t)) a finite separable extension and R^L the finite étale extension of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring with the unique extensions σ_L of σ and d of d/dt. (a) Every (σ_L, ∇)-module M over R^L (∇ relative to d, i.e. Ω^1_{R^L} = R^L dt) is quasi-unipotent: there is a finite separable L'/L (nearly finite separable if k is imperfect) such that M ⊗ R^{L'} is unipotent, and M has a basis of horizontal sections over R^{L'}_log = R^{L'}[log t]. (b) (Transport.) Let A be a topological ring with an endomorphism φ_A, a continuous derivation ∂_A, and a continuous ring isomorphism ι : A → R^L with ι φ_A ι^{−1} = σ_L and ι ∂_A ι^{−1} = u·d/dt for a unit u ∈ (R^L)^×. If (M, F, ∂_M) is a finite free A-module with a φ_A-semilinear F whose linearisation is bijective and a derivation ∂_M over ∂_A satisfying ∂_M∘F = (u·dσ_L(t)/dt / σ_L(u))·F∘∂_M, then ∇(m) = ∂_M(m) ⊗ dt/u makes ι_*M a (σ_L, ∇)-module, so (a) applies, and the conclusion does not depend on ι. (c) Berger's setting: for K finite over Q_p, Berger's ring B†_rig,K is B†_rig,F ⊗_{B†_F} B†_K (Berger, Lemme 3.13), i.e. the ring R^L for the finite separable extension L of k((π)) attached to K by the field of norms, with ϕ and ∂ = (1+π)d/dπ; taking u = 1 + π, ϕ(1+π) = (1+π)^p gives the factor p, so a module with ∂_M∘ϕ = pϕ∘∂_M is a (ϕ,∇)-module and has a basis of solutions over R^{L'}[log π] (Berger, Théorème 5.20, proved under the standing assumption of his §5.5, p. 57, that k is algebraically closed; (a) needs no such assumption). The identification of B†_K with the unramified extension of B†_F attached to that field-of-norms extension belongs to the p-adic Hodge theory consumer (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3 and its own P7 layer), not to this roadmap.
hypotheses: σ is a Frobenius lift in the sense of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring; its extension σ_L to R^L is unique because R^int_L is étale over R^int and L/k((t)) is separable (so the relative Frobenius of L is bijective).
In (b) the factor u·dσ_L(t)/dt/σ_L(u) is exactly what makes ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ_L)∘∇ hold for ∇ = ∂_M ⊗ dt/u.
proofSteps: (a) Restriction of scalars: π_*M is a finite free R_K-module with connection; since L/k((t)) is separable the square of Frobenius lifts is cocartesian (R^L ⊗_{R_K,σ} R_K ≅ R^L via σ_L), so σ^*(π_*M) = π_*(σ_L^*M) and F induces a Frobenius structure on π_*M.

By RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement π_*M becomes unipotent over R^{L''} for a finite Galois L''/k((t)) which may be taken to contain L; M ⊗ R^{L''} is a direct summand of (π_*M) ⊗ R^{L''} (because R^L ⊗_{R_K} R^{L''} is a product of copies of R^{L''}), and unipotence passes to direct summands (subquotients), so M ⊗ R^{L''} is unipotent.
Log solutions over R^{L''}_log by RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy applied to π_*M and projection to the summand.

(b) Compute ∇(F m) = ∂_M(F m) ⊗ dt/u and (F ⊗ dσ_L)(∂_M m ⊗ dt/u) = F(∂_M m) ⊗ (dσ_L(t)/dt / σ_L(u)) dt; they agree iff ∂_M∘F = (u·dσ_L(t)/dt/σ_L(u))·F∘∂_M. Independence of ι: two presentations differ by a continuous automorphism of R^L commuting with σ_L, and unipotence and horizontal sections are invariant (RD.2/unipotent-differential-module, invariance under change of parameter).

(c) Berger p. 57: Ω^1_{R_K} = R_K dπ_K/π_K, and on R_F dx = (π∂x/(1+π)) dπ/π, so the Frobenius compatibility of the connection is ∂_M∘ϕ = pϕ∘∂_M; finitely presented modules with connection are free (RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free).
acceptance: L = k((t)): (a) is RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement itself.
Berger's setting with K = Q_p: L = F_p((π)), B†_rig,Q_p = R_{Q_p} in π with ϕ(π) = (1+π)^p − 1 and ∂ = (1+π)d/dπ; the compatibility factor is u·dϕ(π)/dπ/ϕ(u) = (1+π)·p(1+π)^{p−1}/(1+π)^p = p.
Dwork's module over R^L for L the Artin-Schreier extension of t^{−1}: already constant, L' = L.

sources.match: R^L = R ⊗_{E†} E†_L for finite separable L to which φ extends, quasiconstant and quasiunipotent modules over R, and the p-adic local monodromy theorem (Theorem 20.1.4): a finite free differential module over R admitting a Frobenius structure for some Frobenius lift is quasi-unipotent.

sources.locator: Definition 24.2.7, p. 360; Theorem 24.4.4 and Corollary 24.4.5, p. 363
sources.match: B†_rig,K = B†_K ⊗_{B†_{Q_p}} R and Berger's theorem that de Rham representations are potentially semistable, obtained by applying Theorem 20.1.4.

B†_rig,K = B†_rig,F ⊗_{B†_F} B†_K; §5.5 assumes from p. 57 on that k is algebraically closed; the finite extensions R_K = B†_rig,K come from finite separable extensions of k((π)) by the field of norms; Frobenius compatibility ∂_M∘ϕ = pϕ∘∂_M; every finitely presented differential module with Frobenius structure has a basis of solutions in R′[log π] for a finite étale R′.

nodes.title: The completion of an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed, in every characteristic
nodes.statement: Let F be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, F̄ an algebraic closure with the unique extension of the absolute value, and C_F the completion of F̄. Then C_F is algebraically closed. More generally, if L is a complete nonarchimedean field containing a dense algebraically closed subfield, then L is algebraically closed. In particular, for F = k((t)) (characteristic p) the completed algebraic closure ℓ^alg used for the extended Robba ring (RD.0/extended-robba-ring) is algebraically closed, hence perfect.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on the characteristic: Mathlib's IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange is proved only for complete fields of characteristic 0 (it uses Krasner's lemma, which needs separability); the argument below uses continuity of roots instead.
proofSteps: Let f ∈ C_F[X] be monic of degree n ≥ 1. Approximate f by monic polynomials f_j ∈ F̄[X] of degree n with coefficients converging to those of f (Mathlib Polynomial.exists_monic_and_natDegree_eq_and_norm_map_algebraMap_coeff_sub_lt, using density of F̄).
Each f_j has a root r_j ∈ F̄; the r_j are bounded by C = max |a_i|^{1/(n−i)} and |f(r_j)| ≤ max_i |a_i − a_{ij}|·max(1, C^{n−1}) → 0 (Conrad, Math 248A handout, §2).

In a splitting field L of f over C_F (with the spectral norm extending the absolute value, Mathlib spectralNorm.normedField and spectralNorm_extends), f = Π (X − ρ_k), so Π_k |r_j − ρ_k| → 0; by pigeonhole a subsequence of the r_j converges to one root ρ_k (compare Mathlib Polynomial.exists_aroots_norm_sub_lt_of_norm_coeff_sub_lt, which needs no separability).
That subsequence is Cauchy in the complete field C_F, so its limit lies in C_F and is a root of f; hence C_F is algebraically closed (Mathlib IsAlgClosed.of_exists_root).

Perfectness: in an algebraically closed field every element has a p-th root (Mathlib IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq), so it is perfect (Mathlib PerfectField; the instance IsAlgClosed.perfectField at the pin).
acceptance: Characteristic 0: C_p = completion of Q̄_p is algebraically closed (Mathlib PadicComplex.isAlgClosed), recovered by this argument.
Characteristic p: the completion of the algebraic closure of F_p((t)) is algebraically closed although F_p((t))^alg is not complete and has infinite degree over F_p((t)) (Conrad, §1).

Non-example: F̄ itself is not complete when [F̄ : F] is infinite (Conrad, §1, citing Bosch-Güntzer-Remmert 3.4.3/1), so completing is necessary; and a complete discretely valued field such as k((t)) is never algebraically closed (Eisenstein polynomials X^e − t).

sources.match: The completion of an algebraic closure of a complete nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed, proved by approximating a monic polynomial by ones over the algebraic closure and extracting a Cauchy subsequence of their roots, with no characteristic assumption.

Kedlaya works with Γ^alg over the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (as opposed to the uncompleted one of the monodromy paper), using that this complete field is algebraically closed without giving a reference.

sourceIssues.printed: For V with finite local monodromy and ρ close to 1, the generic radius R(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) is said to equal ρ^b, with b the largest i ≥ 1 such that the upper ramification group G^i is not contained in the kernel; Corollary 19.4.2 says the same of the subsidiary radii.
